excerpt: To facilitate the effective implementation of this policy across the company, we commit to the following:
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to a set of internal governance measures to support effective implementation of the policy.

excerpt: Responsible Scaling Officer: We will maintain the position of Responsible Scaling Officer, a designated member of staff who is responsible for reducing catastrophic risk, primarily by ensuring this policy is designed and implemented effectively.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain a Responsible Scaling Officer role responsible for reducing catastrophic risk through effective policy implementation.

context_stem: The Responsible Scaling Officer's duties will include (but are not limited to):
excerpt: (1) as needed, proposing updates to this policy to the Board of Directors; (2) approving relevant model training or deployment decisions based on capability and safeguard assessments; (3) reviewing major contracts (i.e., deployment partnerships) for consistency with this policy;
paraphrase: The RSO's duties include proposing policy updates, approving training/deployment decisions, and reviewing major contracts for policy consistency.

context_stem: The Responsible Scaling Officer's duties will include (but are not limited to):
excerpt: (4) overseeing implementation of this policy, including the allocation of sufficient resources; (5) receiving and addressing reports of potential instances of noncompliance; (6) promptly notifying the Board of Directors of any cases of noncompliance that pose material risk; and (7) making judgment calls on policy interpretation and application.
paraphrase: The RSO's duties also include overseeing implementation and resourcing, handling noncompliance reports, notifying the Board of material noncompliance, and making interpretive judgment calls.

excerpt: We consider implementation of the ASL-3 Security Standard alone sufficient to continue training, regardless of whether the ASL-3 Deployment Standard is satisfied. "Comparable or greater capabilities" is operationalized as 1x or more in Effective Compute.
paraphrase: A footnote clarifies that ASL-3 Security Standard alone suffices to continue training and defines comparable capability as 1x or more Effective Compute.

excerpt: In addition to noncompliance processes, we will (1) establish pathways for Anthropic staff to raise any issues related to this policy, including the overall risk levels of our models and implementation challenges; and (2) regularly review our compliance with this policy's procedural requirements.
paraphrase: Beyond noncompliance handling, Anthropic will create staff channels to raise policy-related issues and will regularly review compliance with procedural requirements.

excerpt: Cases deemed to present minimal additional risk may be reported to the Board in quarterly summary reports.
paraphrase: Low-risk noncompliance cases may instead be reported quarterly in summary to the Board.

excerpt: In cases where this policy is unintentionally ambiguous, we will act in accordance with the Responsible Scaling Officer or CEO's judgment, and aim to clarify the ambiguity in the next policy update.
paraphrase: Ambiguities in the policy will be resolved via RSO or CEO judgment, with clarification intended for the next update.

excerpt: Readiness: We will develop internal safety procedures for incident scenarios. Such scenarios include (1) pausing training in response to reaching Capability Thresholds; (2) responding to a security incident involving model weights; and (3) responding to severe jailbreaks or vulnerabilities in deployed models, including restricting access in safety emergencies that cannot otherwise be mitigated.
paraphrase: Anthropic will develop internal procedures for incident scenarios including training pauses, weight security incidents, and severe jailbreaks or vulnerabilities.

excerpt: We will run exercises to ensure our readiness for incident scenarios.
paraphrase: Anthropic will conduct exercises to test readiness for incident scenarios.

excerpt: Transparency: We will share summaries of Capability Reports and Safeguards Reports with Anthropic's regular-clearance staff, redacting any highly-sensitive information. We will share a minimally redacted version of these reports with a subset of staff, to help us surface relevant technical safety considerations.
paraphrase: Anthropic will share redacted report summaries broadly with staff and minimally redacted versions with a subset of staff to surface safety considerations.

excerpt: Internal review: For each Capabilities or Safeguards Report, we will solicit feedback from internal teams with visibility into the relevant activities, with the aims of informing future refinements to our methodology and, in some circumstances, identifying weaknesses and informing the CEO and RSO's decisions.
paraphrase: Anthropic will solicit internal feedback on each report to refine methodology and inform CEO/RSO decisions.

excerpt: Noncompliance: We will maintain a process through which Anthropic staff may anonymously notify the Responsible Scaling Officer of any potential instances of noncompliance with this policy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain an anonymous reporting process for potential noncompliance directed to the RSO.

excerpt: We will also establish a policy governing noncompliance reporting, which will (1) protect reporters from retaliation and (2) set forth a mechanism for escalating reports to one or more members of the Board of Directors in cases where the report relates to conduct of the Responsible Scaling Officer.
paraphrase: A noncompliance reporting policy will protect reporters and provide escalation to the Board when reports concern the RSO's own conduct.

excerpt: Further, we will track and investigate any reported or otherwise identified potential instances of noncompliance with this policy. Where reports are substantiated, we will take appropriate and proportional corrective action and document the same.
paraphrase: Anthropic will track, investigate, and take documented corrective action on substantiated noncompliance reports.

excerpt: The Responsible Scaling Officer will regularly update the Board of Directors on substantial cases of noncompliance and overall trends.
paraphrase: The RSO will regularly brief the Board on substantial noncompliance cases and general trends.

excerpt: Employee agreements: We will not impose contractual non-disparagement obligations on employees, candidates, or former employees in a way that could impede or discourage them from publicly raising safety concerns about Anthropic.
paraphrase: Anthropic will not use non-disparagement clauses to discourage employees from raising safety concerns publicly.

excerpt: If we offer agreements with a non-disparagement clause, that clause will not preclude raising safety concerns, nor will it preclude disclosure of the existence of that clause.
paraphrase: Any non-disparagement clause offered will permit raising safety concerns and disclosing the clause's existence.

excerpt: Policy changes: Changes to this policy will be proposed by the CEO and the Responsible Scaling Officer and approved by the Board of Directors, in consultation with the Long-Term Benefit Trust.
paraphrase: Policy changes are proposed by the CEO and RSO and approved by the Board in consultation with the Long-Term Benefit Trust.

excerpt: The current version of the RSP is accessible at www.anthropic.com/rsp. We will update the public version of the RSP before any changes take effect and record any differences from the prior draft in a change log.
paraphrase: The current RSP is published online, with updates to the public version made before changes take effect and differences logged.

excerpt: It is possible at some point in the future that another actor in the frontier AI ecosystem will pass, or be on track to imminently pass, a Capability Threshold without implementing measures equivalent to the Required Safeguards such that their actions pose a serious risk for the world.
paraphrase: The footnote raises the scenario of another frontier AI actor passing a Capability Threshold without equivalent safeguards, posing serious risk.

excerpt: In such a scenario, because the incremental increase in risk attributable to us would be small, we might decide to lower the Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: In that scenario Anthropic might lower its Required Safeguards since its own incremental risk contribution would be small.

excerpt: If we take this measure, however, we will also acknowledge the overall level of risk posed by AI systems (including ours), and will invest significantly in making a case to the U.S. government for taking regulatory action to mitigate such risk to acceptable levels.
paraphrase: If Anthropic lowers safeguards in this scenario, it will also acknowledge overall AI risk and advocate to the U.S. government for regulatory action.

excerpt: We currently expect that if we do not deploy the model publicly and instead proceed with training or limited deployments, we will likely instead share evaluation details with a relevant U.S. Government entity.
paraphrase: If a model is not publicly deployed, Anthropic expects to share evaluation details with a U.S. Government entity instead.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: To advance the public dialogue on the regulation of frontier AI model risks and to enable examination of our actions, we commit to the following:
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to transparency measures to advance public dialogue and enable scrutiny of its actions.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: Public disclosures: We will publicly release key information related to the evaluation and deployment of our models (not including sensitive details). These include summaries of related Capability and Safeguards reports when we deploy a model as well as plans for current and future comprehensive capability assessments and deployment and security safeguards.
paraphrase: Anthropic will publicly release key non-sensitive evaluation and deployment information, including report summaries and plans for assessments and safeguards.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: We will also periodically release information on internal reports of potential instances of non-compliance and other implementation challenges we encounter.
paraphrase: Anthropic will periodically publish information on internal noncompliance reports and implementation challenges.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: Expert input: We will solicit input from external experts in relevant domains in the process of developing and conducting capability and safeguards assessments.
paraphrase: Anthropic will solicit external expert input while developing and conducting capability and safeguards assessments.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: We may also solicit external expert input prior to making final decisions on the capability and safeguards assessments.
paraphrase: Anthropic may also seek external expert input before finalizing capability and safeguards assessment decisions.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: U.S. Government notice: We will notify a relevant U.S. Government entity if a model requires stronger protections than the ASL-2 Standard.
paraphrase: Anthropic will notify the U.S. Government if a model requires protections stronger than ASL-2.
stated_bar: stronger protections than the ASL-2 Standard

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: Procedural compliance review: On approximately an annual basis, we will commission a third-party review that assesses whether we adhered to this policy's main procedural commitments (we expect to iterate on the exact list since this has not been done before for RSPs).
paraphrase: Anthropic will commission an approximately annual third-party review of adherence to the policy's procedural commitments.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: This review will focus on procedural compliance, not substantive outcomes. We will also do such reviews internally on a more regular cadence.
paraphrase: The third-party review focuses on procedure not outcomes, and internal reviews will occur more frequently.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: These will be posted to www.anthropic.com/rsp-updates. We anticipate providing updates at least every 6-12 months.
paraphrase: Updates will be posted online, anticipated at least every 6-12 months.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: Where possible, we will include descriptions of the empirical evaluation results we believe would indicate that a model is no longer safe to store under the ASL-2 Standard.
paraphrase: Where possible, updates will describe evaluation results indicating a model is no longer safe under ASL-2.

section_heading: 7. Governance and Transparency / 7.2. Transparency and External Input
excerpt: Our purpose in these updates is to provide sufficient detail to facilitate conversations about best practices for safeguards, capability evaluations, and elicitation.
paraphrase: The purpose of these updates is to provide detail supporting discussions of best practices in safeguards and evaluation.

excerpt: Technical and operational standards for safely training and deploying frontier AI models. Higher ASLs correspond to stronger safety and security measures required for more capable models.
paraphrase: ASLs are defined as standards for safe training and deployment, scaling in stringency with model capability.

excerpt: The current default standard for all Anthropic models, including security measures, safety testing, and automated misuse detection.
paraphrase: ASL-2 is the default standard covering security, safety testing, and automated misuse detection for all models.

excerpt: A higher level of safeguards required when a model cannot be certified as ASL-2 appropriate. It includes more stringent security and deployment measures designed to mitigate risks from more capable models.
paraphrase: ASL-3 is a stricter safeguard tier triggered when ASL-2 certification is not possible, involving stronger security and deployment measures.

excerpt: A document attesting that a model is sufficiently far from each of the relevant Capability Thresholds, and therefore (still) appropriate for storing under an ASL-N Standard. It includes evaluation procedures, results, and other relevant evidence gathered around the time of testing.
paraphrase: A Capability Report attests a model remains sufficiently below Capability Thresholds for its ASL-N Standard, documenting evaluation methods and evidence.

excerpt: Specific AI capabilities that, if reached, would require stronger safeguards than the current baseline ASL-N standard provides.
paraphrase: Capability Thresholds are specific capability levels that trigger stronger safeguards than the current baseline.

excerpt: A scaling trend-based metric that accounts for both FLOPs and algorithmic improvements.
paraphrase: Effective Compute is a metric combining FLOPs and algorithmic improvement trends.

excerpt: Empirical tests designed to provide early warning when a model is approaching a Capability Threshold. These tests are intended to trigger before a model actually reaches a dangerous capability.
paraphrase: Evaluations are empirical tests intended to give early warning before a model reaches a dangerous capability.

excerpt: Floating-Point Operation(s). The amount of computation required to train or run a model. The number of FLOPs can be used as one indicator of a model's computational complexity and, indirectly, its potential capabilities.
paraphrase: FLOPs measure computation used to train or run a model and can indicate computational complexity and potential capability.

excerpt: Anthropic's Board of Directors approves the RSP and receives Capability Reports and Safeguards Reports. The LTBT is an external body that is consulted on policy changes and also provided with Capability Reports and Safeguards Reports.
paraphrase: The Board approves the RSP and receives reports; the LTBT is an external body consulted on changes and also given reports.

excerpt: More details about the LTBT are available here.
paraphrase: Further LTBT details are referenced as available elsewhere.

excerpt: The standard of safety and security measures that must be implemented when a model reaches a Capability Threshold.
paraphrase: Required Safeguards are the mandated safety and security measures triggered at a Capability Threshold.

excerpt: A designated staff member responsible for reducing catastrophic risk, primarily by ensuring this policy is designed and implemented effectively. Their duties include reviewing policy updates, approving reports, overseeing implementation, and approving deployments.
paraphrase: The RSO is a staff member accountable for catastrophic risk reduction via effective policy design and implementation, with duties spanning review, approvals, and oversight.

excerpt: A document attesting that the implemented safeguards meet an ASL-N Standard. It details the design and planned implementation of safeguards, and evidence to demonstrate their expected effectiveness.
paraphrase: A Safeguards Report attests implemented safeguards meet an ASL-N Standard, with details of design and evidence of effectiveness.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Deployment Standard / bullet 1
excerpt: Acceptable use policies and model cards: Publication of model cards for significant new models describing capabilities, limitations, evaluations, and intended use cases.
paraphrase: ASL-2 deployment requires publishing model cards for significant new models covering capabilities, limitations, evaluations, and intended use.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Deployment Standard / bullet 1
excerpt: Enforcement of a Usage Policy that restricts, at a minimum, catastrophic and high harm use cases, including using the model to generate content that could cause severe risks to the continued existence of humankind, or direct and severe harm to individuals.
paraphrase: A Usage Policy must at minimum restrict catastrophic and high-harm uses, including content risking humanity's existence or severe individual harm.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Deployment Standard / bullet 2
excerpt: Harmlessness training and automated detection: Training models to refuse requests to aid in causing harm, such as with Constitutional AI or other improved techniques, and the use of model enhanced trust and safety detection and enforcement.
paraphrase: Models are trained to refuse harmful requests via techniques like Constitutional AI, supported by automated trust and safety detection.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Deployment Standard / bullet 3
excerpt: Fine-tuning protections: In finetuning products, data is filtered for harmfulness, and models are subject to automated evaluation to check harmlessness features are not degraded.
paraphrase: Fine-tuning products filter harmful data and undergo automated checks to preserve harmlessness features.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Deployment Standard / bullet 3
excerpt: There are a very limited number of use cases where this tooling is disabled. These are negotiated on a case by case basis and considered only for extremely low risk use cases that involve company personnel.
paraphrase: Disabling fine-tuning safety tooling is rare, negotiated case-by-case, and limited to extremely low-risk internal use cases.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Deployment Standard / bullet 4
excerpt: Vulnerability reporting channels: Clearly indicated paths within the product for users to report harmful or dangerous model outputs, as well as a bug bounty for universal jailbreaks.
paraphrase: The product must provide clear reporting paths for harmful outputs and a bug bounty for universal jailbreaks.

excerpt: ASL-2 Security Standard: A security system that can likely thwart most opportunistic attackers.
paraphrase: The ASL-2 Security Standard is described as capable of thwarting most opportunistic attackers.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Security Standard / bullet 1
excerpt: Supply chain: Vendor and supplier security must be regularly reviewed to ensure that they meet security standards. Software updates should be frequently managed and compliance monitoring automated where possible.
paraphrase: Supply chain security requires regular vendor review and frequent, ideally automated, update and compliance management.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Security Standard / bullet 2
excerpt: Offices: Physical security should entail visitor access logs and restrictions protect on-site assets. Highly sensitive interactions should utilize advanced authentication like security keys.
paraphrase: Office security should include visitor logs, access restrictions, and advanced authentication such as security keys for sensitive interactions.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Security Standard / bullet 2
excerpt: Network visibility should be maintained and office access controls and communications should maximize on-site protections.
paraphrase: Network visibility and office access/communications controls should maximize on-site protection.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Security Standard / bullet 3
excerpt: Workforce: People-critical processes must represent a key aspect of cybersecurity. Mandatory periodic infosec training educates all employees on secure practices, like proper system configurations and strong passwords, and fosters a proactive "security mindset."
paraphrase: Workforce security requires mandatory periodic training on secure practices to build a proactive security mindset.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Security Standard / bullet 3
excerpt: Fundamental infrastructure and policies promoting secure-by-design and secure-by-default principles should be incorporated into the engineering process. An insider risk program should tie access to job roles. Rapid incident response protocols must be deployed.
paraphrase: Engineering should incorporate secure-by-design principles, an insider risk program tying access to roles, and rapid incident response protocols.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Security Standard / bullet 4
excerpt: Compartmentalization: Segmented system isolation must ensure limited blast radius. Features like zero trust architecture should require access from approved devices.
paraphrase: Compartmentalization requires segmented isolation limiting blast radius and zero trust architecture requiring approved-device access.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Security Standard / bullet 4
excerpt: Strict protocols must be deployed to regulate weight copies on company networks and limit storage to only approved, restricted systems.
paraphrase: Strict protocols must regulate weight copies on company networks and restrict storage to approved systems.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Security Standard / bullet 5
excerpt: Infrastructure: Standard security infrastructure, monitoring software, access management tools, and disk encryption provide a technology baseline.
paraphrase: Infrastructure security baseline includes standard monitoring, access management, and disk encryption.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Security Standard / bullet 5
excerpt: Process elements like incident reporting procedures, lost/stolen device protocols and Detection and Response should support these.
paraphrase: Process elements such as incident reporting and lost/stolen device protocols should support the infrastructure baseline.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Security Standard / bullet 5
excerpt: External validation like SOC 2 compliance and continuous vulnerability management must ensure adaptations match infosec developments. Programs like bug bounties and vulnerability discovery should incentivize exposing flaws.
paraphrase: External validation such as SOC 2 and continuous vulnerability management must keep pace with infosec developments, supplemented by bug bounty programs.

locator: App B / ASL-2 Security Standard / bullet 6
excerpt: Operations: Ongoing configuration management, compliance drills, integrated security approaches and mandatory external reviews should embed security within regular operations and harden processes during organizational changes.
paraphrase: Operations should embed configuration management, compliance drills, integrated security, and mandatory external reviews into regular processes and organizational change.

excerpt: This appendix contains detailed definitions for each Capability Threshold in Section 2.
paraphrase: The appendix provides detailed definitions for Capability Thresholds referenced elsewhere.

excerpt: Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) weapons: The ability to significantly assist individuals or groups with basic STEM backgrounds in obtaining, producing, or deploying CBRN weapons.
paraphrase: The CBRN threshold is defined as significant assistance to basic-STEM individuals or groups in obtaining, producing, or deploying CBRN weapons.

excerpt: We assess this by comparing what potential attackers could achieve with full model access versus 2023-level online resources, assuming they have funding and up to one year of time to invest, but no initial specialized expertise.
paraphrase: Assessment compares attacker capability with full model access versus 2023-level online resources, assuming funding and up to a year of effort but no prior expertise.
stated_bar: up to one year of time

excerpt: We are uncertain how to choose a specific threshold, but we maintain a current list of specific CBRN capabilities of concern for which we would implement stronger mitigations.
paraphrase: Despite uncertainty on precise thresholds, Anthropic maintains a list of concerning CBRN capabilities warranting stronger mitigations.

excerpt: We treat these lists as sensitive, but we plan to share them with organizations such as AI Safety Institutes and the Frontier Model Forum, and keep these lists updated.
paraphrase: The sensitive CBRN capability lists are planned to be shared with bodies like AI Safety Institutes and the Frontier Model Forum, and kept up to date.

excerpt: This comparison is hard to make in practice; this note is to clarify the meaning of the conceptual threshold and the fact that this policy aims to measure risk relative to the world in 2023, so that we can understand how much risk the current generations of frontier models are creating.
paraphrase: The footnote clarifies the comparison is difficult in practice and the threshold measures risk relative to a 2023 baseline.

excerpt: Autonomous AI Research and Development: The ability to either: (1) Fully automate the work of an entry-level remote-only Researcher at Anthropic, as assessed by performance on representative tasks or (2) cause dramatic acceleration in the rate of effective scaling.
paraphrase: The Autonomous AI R&D threshold covers either full automation of an entry-level researcher's work or causing dramatic acceleration in effective scaling rates.

excerpt: Specifically, this would be the case if we observed or projected an increase in the effective training compute of the world's most capable model that, over the course of a year, was equivalent to two years of the average rate of progress during the period of early 2018 to early 2024.
paraphrase: This threshold is triggered by an observed or projected year of scaling equivalent to two years of the 2018-2024 average progress rate.
stated_bar: two years of the average rate of progress during 2018 to 2024

excerpt: We roughly estimate that the 2018-2024 average scaleup was around 35x per year, so this would imply an actual or projected one-year scaleup of 35^2 = ~1000x.
paraphrase: Given an estimated 35x/year average scaleup, the threshold implies roughly a 1000x one-year scaleup.

excerpt: Model Autonomy checkpoint: The ability to perform a wide range of advanced software engineering tasks autonomously that could be precursors to full autonomous replication or automated AI R&D, and that would take a domain expert human 2-8 hours to complete.
paraphrase: The Model Autonomy checkpoint covers autonomous performance of advanced software engineering tasks, taking a human expert 2-8 hours, that could precede full autonomy or automated R&D.

excerpt: We primarily view this level of model autonomy as a checkpoint on the way to managing the risks of robust, fully autonomous systems with capabilities that might include (a) automating and greatly accelerating research and development in AI development (b) generating their own revenue and using it to run copies of themselves in large-scale, hard-to-shut-down operations.
paraphrase: This checkpoint is viewed as a step toward managing risks from fully autonomous systems capable of accelerating AI R&D or self-funding large-scale self-replication.

excerpt: The 35x/year scaleup estimate is based on assuming the rate of increase in compute being used to train frontier models from ~2018 to May 2024 is 4.2 x/year (reference), the impact of increased (LLM) algorithmic efficiency is roughly equivalent to a further 2.8 x/year (reference), and the impact of post training enhancements is a further 3 x/year (informal estimate).
paraphrase: The 35x/year estimate combines a 4.2x/year compute increase, 2.8x/year algorithmic efficiency gain, and 3x/year post-training enhancement.

excerpt: Combined, these have an effective rate of scaling of 35 x/year.
paraphrase: Combined, the estimated factors yield an effective scaling rate of 35x/year.

excerpt: September 19, 2023 RSP-2023 (aka RSP v1.0): Initial version.
paraphrase: The changelog records the initial RSP version dated September 19, 2023.

excerpt: October 15, 2024 RSP-2024: This update introduces a more flexible and nuanced approach to assessing and managing AI risks while maintaining our commitment not to train or deploy models unless we have implemented adequate safeguards.
paraphrase: The October 15, 2024 update introduces a more flexible risk management approach while retaining the commitment to adequate safeguards before training or deployment.

excerpt: Key improvements include new capability thresholds to indicate when we should upgrade our safeguards, refined processes for evaluating model capabilities and the adequacy of our safeguards (inspired by safety case methodologies), and new measures for internal governance and external input.
paraphrase: Key improvements include new capability thresholds, refined evaluation processes inspired by safety cases, and new internal governance and external input measures.

excerpt: We describe the most notable changes below.
paraphrase: The following entries describe the most notable changes.

excerpt: ASL definition changed: The term "ASL" now refers to groups of technical and operational safeguards (it previously also referred to models). We also introduced the new concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: The ASL term now refers only to safeguard groups rather than models, and new concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards were introduced.

excerpt: This change allows for more targeted application of safeguards based on specific capabilities, rather than broad model categories.
paraphrase: The redefinition enables safeguards to be targeted at specific capabilities instead of broad model categories.

locator: Changelog / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: ARA threshold now a checkpoint: We replaced our previous autonomous replication and adaption (ARA) threshold with a "checkpoint" for autonomous AI capabilities.
paraphrase: The former ARA threshold was replaced with a checkpoint concept for autonomous AI capabilities.

locator: Changelog / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: Rather than triggering higher safety standards automatically, reaching this checkpoint will prompt additional evaluation of the model's capabilities and accelerate our preparation of stronger safeguards.
paraphrase: Reaching the checkpoint now triggers additional evaluation and accelerated safeguard preparation rather than automatic escalation.

locator: Changelog / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: We previously considered these capabilities as a trigger for increased safeguards, motivated by an attempt to establish some threshold while we developed a better sense of potential threats.
paraphrase: Previously these capabilities triggered increased safeguards as a provisional threshold pending better threat understanding.

locator: Changelog / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: We now believe that these capabilities - at the levels we initially considered - would not necessitate the ASL-3 standard.
paraphrase: Anthropic now believes these capability levels do not require the ASL-3 standard.

excerpt: AI R&D threshold added: We added a new threshold for AI systems that can significantly advance AI development.
paraphrase: A new threshold was added for AI systems capable of significantly advancing AI development.

excerpt: Such capabilities could lead to rapid, unpredictable advances in AI, potentially outpacing our ability to evaluate and address emerging risks, and may also serve as an early warning sign for the ability to automate R&D in other domains.
paraphrase: These capabilities could drive rapid unpredictable advances outpacing risk evaluation, and may signal broader R&D automation ability.

excerpt: Testing for Capability Thresholds: Rather than using prespecified evaluations, we now require an affirmative case that models are sufficiently far from Capability Thresholds.
paraphrase: Testing now requires an affirmative case of distance from Capability Thresholds rather than reliance on prespecified evaluations.

excerpt: Predefined tests may miss emerging risks or be overly conservative relative to the actual threshold of concern.
paraphrase: Predefined tests risk missing emerging threats or being overly conservative relative to the true threshold.

excerpt: Our most accurate tests change frequently enough that it is more practical to use this new approach than to have our Board of Directors pre-approve evaluations.
paraphrase: Because accurate tests change often, the affirmative-case approach is more practical than requiring Board pre-approval of evaluations.

excerpt: Adjusted evaluation cadence: We adjusted the comprehensive assessment cadence to 4x Effective Compute or six months of accumulated post-training enhancements (this was previously three months).
paraphrase: The comprehensive assessment cadence changed to 4x Effective Compute or six months of post-training enhancements, up from a prior three-month cadence.
stated_bar: 4x Effective Compute or six months (previously three months)

excerpt: We found that a three-month cadence forced teams to prioritize conducting frequent evaluations over more comprehensive testing and improving methodologies.
paraphrase: The prior three-month cadence forced teams to prioritize frequent evaluation over comprehensive testing and methodology improvement.

excerpt: Less prescriptive evaluation methodology: We have replaced some specifics in our previous testing methodology (e.g., using 1% of compute for elicitation or creating a 6x buffer), with more general requirements to (a) match expected efforts of potential adversaries and (b) provide informal estimates of how further scaling and research developments will impact model capabilities and performance on the same tasks.
paraphrase: Specific prior methodology elements like 1% compute for elicitation or a 6x buffer were replaced with general requirements to match adversary effort and estimate future scaling impacts.

excerpt: We have found that specific methodologies may become outdated when new research developments are introduced.
paraphrase: Specific methodologies risk becoming outdated as new research emerges.

excerpt: Although still an aspirational goal, the science of evaluations is not currently mature enough to make confident predictions about the precise buffer we should require between current models and a Capability Threshold.
paraphrase: Precise buffer requirements remain an aspirational goal since evaluation science is not yet mature enough for confident predictions.

excerpt: More outcome-focused safeguard requirements: We have updated our ASL-3 safeguards requirements to be less prescriptive and more outcome-focused.
paraphrase: ASL-3 safeguard requirements were updated to be less prescriptive and more focused on outcomes.

excerpt: Rather than detailing specific operational and technical safeguards, we now specify the overall security or deployment standards and requirements for meeting them. This is to allow us to adapt our safeguards more flexibly as our understanding of risks and possible safeguards improves.
paraphrase: Instead of specifying detailed safeguards, the policy now sets overall standards and requirements, allowing flexible adaptation as understanding improves.

locator: Changelog / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
excerpt: Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models: We have clarified which actors are in and out of scope for the ASL-3 Security Standard.
paraphrase: The update clarifies which actors are in or out of scope for the ASL-3 Security Standard.

locator: Changelog / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
excerpt: We also removed the commitment to protect against scaled attacks and distillation attacks from the ASL-2 Security standard.
paraphrase: The commitment to protect against scaled and distillation attacks was removed from the ASL-2 Security standard.

locator: Changelog / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
excerpt: While distillation remains a concern for more capable models, models stored under ASL-2 safeguards have not yet reached potentially harmful Capability Thresholds.
paraphrase: Distillation still concerns more capable models, but ASL-2-stored models have not reached potentially harmful Capability Thresholds.

locator: Changelog / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
excerpt: Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users: We have updated the ASL-3 Deployment Standard to allow for different levels of safeguards based on deployment context.
paraphrase: The ASL-3 Deployment Standard now allows differing safeguard levels depending on deployment context.

locator: Changelog / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
excerpt: For any general access systems, we still require passing intensive red-teaming. For internal use, safety testing and deployments to sufficiently trusted users, we will instead require a combination of access controls and monitoring.
paraphrase: General access systems still require intensive red-teaming, while internal use and trusted-user deployments require access controls and monitoring instead.

locator: Changelog / New Capability and Safeguards Reports
excerpt: We expect that aggregating all the available evidence about model capabilities will provide decision makers with a more complete picture of the overall level of risk and improve our ability to solicit feedback on our work.

excerpt: Internal and external accountability: We have made a number of changes to our previous "procedural commitments."

excerpt: These include expanding the duties of the Responsible Scaling Officer; adding internal critique and external expert input on capability and safeguard assessments; new procedures related to internal governance; and maintaining a public page for overviews of past Capability and Safeguard Reports, RSP-related updates, and future plans.
paraphrase: Changes include expanded RSO duties, added internal critique and external input on assessments, new internal governance procedures, and a public page for report overviews, updates, and plans.
